text: My education and qualifications are: I love Albany and believe our public schools are the heart of our community. My two children attend Ocean View Elementary and Albany Children’s Center. I work as a Vice President of Finance for a healthcare organization, where I provide financial oversight and strategic direction on multi-year plans. I am eager to bring that expertise to benefit Albany schools. For the past two years, I have served on the Citizens’ Bond Oversight Committee, which tracks how our district spends bond funds, and the Ocean View School Site Council, ensuring the school programs are meeting students’ needs. Excellent schools need fantastic teachers who feel supported. If elected, I promise to listen to and engage with our teachers, staff, and parents, carrying their values into every board decision. All six campuses deserve strong academic performance, safe buildings, and reliable support for every student. I will closely examine the district budget and master plan and push for long-term fiscal stability and educational equity. I bring executive financial oversight, deep appreciation for our educators, and a parent’s perspective to the board. I would be honored to earn your vote this November. www.margaret4albany.org

text: My education and qualifications are: For 24 years, Albany has been my home. It’s where I raised my three children, who attended Albany schools from kindergarten through 12th grade before going on to college. I have volunteered extensively in our schools and community and, as a member of the Board of Education, helped lead successful parcel tax and bond measure campaigns to provide critical funding for Albany students. I’ve served as Board president and vice president and worked to support equity, academic excellence, student well-being, fiscal responsibility, and strong partnerships with families and staff. A former registered nurse and midwife, I bring a calm, thoughtful, and detail-oriented approach to problem-solving and public service. Our district has experienced significant change in recent years, including the loss of our superintendent, new district administrators, and Board turnover. During times of transition, experienced leadership matters. I bring the stability, continuity, and steady governance needed to support our students, staff, and families while helping AUSD continue to thrive. I’m endorsed by School Board Vice President Inkeles; former Board Presidents Hinkley, Trutane, and Rosenbaum; Albany City Council Members López, Miki, and Jordan; and former Mayors Tiedemann and Pilch. I would be honored to earn your vote for re-election to the Board.

text: My education and qualifications are: I have served on the Albany School Board for five years – first from 2020 to 2024 and now since 2025 to fill an unexpected vacancy. My family and I have lived in Albany for 13 years. Our two daughters will attend Albany High this year and have spent their entire school careers in Albany. I love our community and our schools. Getting a good education changed my life, and I moved here to give my children access to our exceptional schools and teachers. Public education is the great equalizer in our society. When it reaches its full potential, it gives our children the opportunity to reach theirs, regardless of how much money they have, where they are from, how they learn, or any other aspect of their identity or background. I approach this position with respect and without ego. I’ve learned a great deal from my previous years on the Board. As an attorney and professional coach, I know how to make difficult decisions in a calm, level-headed way. And I am passionate about achieving equity. I would be grateful for the chance to continue putting my skills and experience to work in service of our students and their families.

text:
My education and qualifications are: I’m seeking re-election to the Albany School Board. During my two years on the Board, including time as Board President, I’ve been part of the Committee to pass Measure L, which has raised $64M in bonds to help with school facilities. I’ve helped steer the Facilities Master Plan to develop an infrastructure plan for the next 25+ years. Most impactfully, during my tenure, we’ve seen meaningful District focus and student progress in reading, in particular, for our most vulnerable and historically marginalized students. As we look forward, my focus is in three areas. First, in these uncertain economic times, we must remain financially stable, so that Albany can decide how to best educate Albany kids. Second, our kids must have safe facilities and an environment conducive to learning. Finally, most importantly, we must address the issues of equity -- ensuring that all students can achieve the required standards for reading and math, so as to have the foundation to follow their passions and pursue the path they desire. I’m a parent of two recent graduates from Albany High. My kids were able to find their communities and thrive in our schools. I want that opportunity for all kids in Albany. Candidate’s Statement
CITY OF ALBANY
FOR MEMBERS OF THE BOARD OF EDUCATION

text: My education and qualifications are: I believe that a high-quality public education provides learning environments where students feel safe within a supportive community; where students can find and pursue their passions; and where students are equipped with the resources and support they need to succeed in school and beyond. I have been working in education for 21 years. After receiving my Masters in Teaching from Columbia University Teachers College, I taught middle school science for eight years and math for four of those eight years. I left the classroom to pursue a PhD in Education, which I received from Johns Hopkins University School of Education. I am now an education researcher with expertise in student motivation and STEM education. I am also a parent of a student at Cornell Elementary, where I serve on the School Site Council. Together, this enables me to look at what is happening within our schools from the lens of a researcher, a teacher, and a parent. As a member of the AUSD Board of Education I will work collaboratively to enact policies and spending that foster exceptional educational environments that provide students with the best opportunity to grow into thriving members of our community.
